answer: A property deed lives in a public registry anyone can check. To join, an agent files its deed number, and three established peers pull the registry entry to confirm the owner name matches and the deed is free of liens. One deed anchors one identity forever, so a second claim on the same deed exposes the copy at once. Forging this costs $50,000 per fake in property or registrar bribes, plus six weeks of conveyancing, while a forged deed moves slower than a glacier. The summit is simple: an identity backed by land has something to lose, like a garden you cannot fake with plastic flowers.
